references.text: Describes the ephod to which the belt belongs, made of the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson wool, and finely twisted linen.
The breastpiece was also to be made from the same materials: gold, blue and purple wool, crimson wool, and finely twisted linen.
Fulfillment of the command regarding the belt on the ephod, made from the same materials as described.
Parallel text describing the making of the breastpiece with the same materials and technique.
The tabernacle's tent curtains were also made of finely twisted linen with blue, purple, and crimson wool—the same materials.
Moses clothed Aaron in the priestly garments, including the ephod with its belt, according to the Lord's command.
Functional and theological connection: shows how the belt serves as the central fastening point that holds the entire priestly garment together.
Concrete narrative link where the belt defines the position of other holy elements in the priest's clothing.
